title: Signed-payload strkey with a 1-byte inner payload whose three padding bytes are 0xff instead of zero
why: SEP-0023 requires the padding of a signed payload to be present and zero; the SEP's own vectors test only absent padding, so a decoder can pass all 30 and still accept non-zero padding.

known_divergences.detail: Executed: v0.7.1 strkey.Decode returns the payload with its 0xff padding instead of an error; v0.7.2 rejects it. Earlier versions were not run.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9S2 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on go v0.7.1; xcc conform run --columns 'go@v0.7.1' --entries 'strkey/synthetic-gap-vectors.signed-payload-nonzero-padding'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: the v16 StrKey decoder (unchanged since 16.0.0) checks the checksum but not the per-type payload rules and returns a payload. The strict decoder exists only on the v17 line, where 17.2.0 and later reject this vector.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9S2 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on js 16.3.0, js 16.3.1 and js 16.4.1

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 17.0.0 and 17.0.1: StrKey decoding of a signed payload returns the payload with its non-zero padding bytes instead of an error. Fixed on main (pull request #1261), not released.
